title: Checkout resilience architecture
chunk_text: The checkout client sends retryable provider failures through capped exponential backoff with full jitter before the payment gateway. Three total attempts are allowed.

title: Payment provider incident runbook
chunk_text: When retry exhaustion spikes, on-call verifies provider health and transient failure rates. Retry limits may only be changed through the approved feature flag procedure.

title: Checkout retry product behavior
chunk_text: Customers should see at most three payment attempts. The bounded policy reduces duplicate charge risk and prevents long checkout waits.

title: Shared retry library proposal
chunk_text: The Platform team is building a shared retry library with exponential backoff, jitter, metrics, and policy-based maximum attempts for service clients.

title: Add jitter to checkout retries
chunk_text: PAY-123 is In Progress and assigned to Demo Engineer. Add full jitter and unit tests to the checkout retry client.

title: Retry observability standard
chunk_text: All retry loops emit attempt count, terminal outcome, provider, and jitter delay metrics. Alerts distinguish retry exhaustion from permanent declines.

title: Payment data handling policy
chunk_text: Logs and agent prompts must not contain card numbers, tokens, credentials, or full payment payloads. Operational evidence is redacted before storage.

title: Mobile offline payment queue
chunk_text: The Mobile team retries network submission with jitter but never retries a payment after an ambiguous provider acknowledgement.

title: Capped exponential backoff
chunk_text: Adopt full jitter and cap checkout at three total attempts. The governing decision supersedes fixed-delay retry behavior.

title: Checkout failure analysis
chunk_text: Transient provider errors account for most recoverable checkout failures. A third attempt recovers little additional traffic compared with its latency cost.

title: Standardize retry policies
chunk_text: Platform is evaluating a company-wide retry SDK so Payments, Orders, and Notifications do not implement different jitter algorithms.

title: Protected retry design
chunk_text: This cross-tenant document must never be returned to the demo tenant.

title: Payment event delivery architecture
chunk_text: Payment events use an outbox and idempotent consumers. Delivery is at least once, so every consumer stores the event identifier before applying side effects.

title: Payment queue backlog runbook
chunk_text: If payment event lag exceeds ten minutes, pause nonessential consumers, confirm database headroom, and scale the settlement consumer before replaying dead letters.

title: Refund experience requirements
chunk_text: Refund status must be visible within one minute and include the expected settlement window. Support should see the same canonical status as the customer.

title: Payment token lifecycle policy
chunk_text: Payment tokens are scoped to merchant and environment. Rotation must overlap for twenty-four hours and audit logs may contain only token fingerprints.

title: Mobile checkout integration guide
chunk_text: Mobile clients create an idempotency key before submission and retain it until a terminal checkout state is observed.

title: Duplicate charge support playbook
chunk_text: Support checks provider references and the idempotency ledger before escalating a suspected duplicate charge to Payments on-call.

title: Payment idempotency ledger
chunk_text: Store idempotency keys and terminal outcomes for seven days in the regional ledger. Duplicate requests return the original outcome.

title: Checkout latency budget
chunk_text: The p95 checkout authorization target is 2.5 seconds. Retry delay and provider latency are reported separately by region.

title: Introduce event schema registry
chunk_text: Platform is adding compatibility checks for payment and order event schemas before producers can deploy.

title: Settlement mismatch runbook
chunk_text: Compare the internal ledger, provider settlement file, and reconciliation checkpoint. Never replay settlements until the mismatch class is confirmed.

title: Checkout threat model
chunk_text: Replay protection combines idempotency keys, signed provider callbacks, nonce validation, and a bounded acceptance window.

title: Provider failover experience
chunk_text: Automatic provider failover is allowed only before an ambiguous acknowledgement. The UI must not expose provider names to customers.

title: Payments capacity checklist
chunk_text: Before peak traffic, validate database connection budgets, queue drain rates, provider quotas, and regional failover dashboards.

title: Mobile payments SDK 4.2
chunk_text: Version 4.2 adds durable idempotency keys, structured retry metrics, and cancellation-safe checkout resumption.

title: Payments escalation guide
chunk_text: Escalate active authorization incidents to Payments on-call and settlement discrepancies to Finance Operations with the provider reference attached.

title: Payments telemetry architecture
chunk_text: Checkout trace context propagates through gateway, provider adapter, outbox, and settlement consumers without recording payment payloads.

title: Reconcile delayed provider callbacks
chunk_text: Delayed callbacks are matched to the authorization ledger and cannot overwrite a newer terminal payment state.

title: Accessible checkout messaging
chunk_text: Checkout errors use concise text, announce updates to assistive technology, and preserve user input whenever retry is safe.
